status: complete: no_shift (new park-case stop rate 42% vs old 28% vs none 25%); no overcorrection; grader agreement 100%
question: Do the trimmed skill's verdict definitions turn cases that should be parked into investigations, in recommended action or only in label?
scenarios: scenarios/*.txt: six park cases (p1-p6) where existing evidence already decides against investing, and three investigate cases (i1-i3) where parking would be premature

grader.prompt: grader-prompt.md; the grader sees the question and one anonymised answer, never the key, arm or expected verdict
grader.sessions: 162, plus a seeded 20% subset graded a second time to measure classification agreement

measures.primary: Park-case stop rate per arm, pooled across models (36 answers per arm)
secondary: Investigate-case research_first rate per arm (overcorrection check)
Proposed research days before decision on park cases
Grader agreement on the duplicate subset

decision_rules.substantive_shift: new park-case stop rate at least 20 points below old: the verdict definitions change recommendations; revise them and confirm on new scenarios
decision_rules.label_only: stop rates within 20 points but new park-label rate at least 20 points below old: wording changes labels, not actions; a label clarification is optional
decision_rules.no_shift: neither: no evidence the definitions turn park cases into investigations
decision_rules.overcorrection_guard: In every case, report whether new investigate-case research_first rate is at least 20 points below old
decision_rules.grader_reliability: If duplicate-subset action agreement is below 85%, report results as unreliable

power_note: 36 answers per arm on park cases detect differences of roughly 25 points or more
stopping_rule: One attempt per session. Stop on authentication or quota block; resume blocked sessions after reset with identical inputs, keeping the blocked records. No edits to scenarios, key, grader prompt or skill while sessions run.
limits: Model grader classifying action; agreement measured only by repeat grading
